goal: WizTry is a portable, read-only disk space analyzer in the style of WizTree (diskanalyzer.com): pick a folder, scan it fast, and see where the space went in a folder tree, a file-type list and a squarified treemap. Python 3.11 with tkinter, standard library only in the app; PyInstaller packs it into one dist\WizTry.exe. It never deletes, moves, renames or writes anything it scans.
rules: Read-only: the app never deletes, moves, renames or writes any file it scans.
Standard library only in wiztry/ (tkinter, os, stat, threading, json, argparse, dataclasses, datetime, time). PyInstaller is only for build.bat.
Names, signatures, return values, column names and exact strings are the ones in the brief and the tests.
Import between modules as `from wiztry.<module> import <names>`; never copy code from another module.
Tkinter is only touched from the main thread. A background thread may set plain attributes; the main thread polls them with after().
conventions: Python 3.11: type hints on public functions, one-line docstring on every public function and class.
Four-space indents, double quotes, lines under 120 characters.
Run a task's test with: .venv\Scripts\python.exe tests\<file>.py (it prints PASS/FAIL lines; the fixture folders are {FIXTURE} and {FIXTURE_BIG}).
Scratch files and experiments go in the system temp folder, never in the project folder.

tasks.title: The scanner
tasks.brief:
Create the package (wiztry/__init__.py with a one-line docstring) and wiztry/scanner.py.
- REPARSE_POINT = 0x400.
- @dataclass(eq=False) class Node: name: str, path: str, is_dir: bool, size: int = 0, files: int = 0, folders: int = 0, mtime: float = 0.0, children: list (default empty), parent: Node | None = None (repr=False). A folder's size/files/folders cover everything inside it; a file has files=1.
- ext_of(name) -> lower-case extension with its dot (os.path.splitext), or "(none)".
- scan(root, progress=None, cancel=None) -> (top Node, skipped). root = os.path.abspath(root); top.name = its last path part. Walk with an explicit stack and os.scandir (never os.walk). For each entry use e.stat(follow_symlinks=False): skip it entirely if st.st_file_attributes & REPARSE_POINT (junctions and symlinks are neither followed nor counted); a folder (stat.S_ISDIR) becomes a Node pushed on the stack; a file becomes a Node with size=st_size, files=1. Set mtime from the stat, and parent. A folder that cannot be opened (OSError) adds 1 to skipped. Call progress(n) every 2,000 files. If cancel() returns true, stop walking. Afterwards add sizes up from the deepest folders to the top (folders count: child folders + their folders), and sort each children list by (-size, lower-case name).
- summary(top, skipped=0, seconds=0.0) -> dict with root (top.path), total_size, files, folders, skipped, seconds (rounded to 3 places), by_ext (dict sorted by extension: {ext: {"size": ..., "files": ...}} over every file) and top_level ([{"name", "size", "files", "folders"} for each child of top, in children order]).
- timed_scan(root, progress=None, cancel=None) -> (top, skipped, seconds) using time.perf_counter.
Speed matters: the test wants 50,000 files in under 0.6 s and at least 4x faster than os.walk + lstat. The size Windows returns with the directory listing (DirEntry.stat) needs no extra system call.

tasks.title: The treemap layout
tasks.brief:
Pure functions, no drawing, in wiztry/treemap.py.
- squarify(sizes, x, y, w, h) -> list of (x, y, w, h) or None, one per size in the same order. Sizes come largest first. Zero sizes get None; an empty list or a box with no room gives all None (or []). Use the squarified algorithm (Bruls, Huizing, van Wijk): scale sizes to areas that fill w*h; add items to the current row while the worst aspect ratio does not get worse, then lay the row along the shorter side (rows down the left when w >= h, along the top otherwise) and continue in the space left.
- layout(node, x, y, w, h, min_px=3, depth=0) -> list of (child, (x, y, w, h), depth) for every child of node with size > 0 whose block is at least min_px in both directions, in children order; after a folder's own entry, recurse into it with the box shrunk by 1 px on each side and depth + 1, when it is more than 2*min_px in both directions.

tasks.title: File types, colors and sizes
tasks.brief:
wiztry/filetypes.py:
- PALETTE: exactly 20 different #rrggbb colors; OTHER = "#a0a0a0" (not in the palette).
- human(n): below 1024 -> "<n> bytes"; otherwise divide by 1024 into KB, MB, GB, TB with one decimal ("1.5 KB"); TB is the largest unit ("5000.0 TB").
- ext_rows(by_ext) -> list of {"ext", "size", "files", "pct", "color"} sorted by (-size, ext); pct = share of the total size in percent; the first 20 rows take PALETTE in order, the rest OTHER. An empty dict gives [].
- color_map(by_ext) -> {ext: color} as ext_rows assigns them.

tasks.title: Command-line report
tasks.brief:
- wiztry/cli.py: main(argv=None) -> int. argparse with --scan (required, a folder) and --json (required, the report file). Run timed_scan, write summary(top, skipped, seconds) as JSON (indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, utf-8). Print nothing. Return 0.
- WizTry.py at the top of the project: under `if __name__ == "__main__":`, if "--scan" is in sys.argv, sys.exit(cli main(sys.argv[1:])); otherwise import wiztry.app's main and call it (wiztry.app does not exist yet, so import it only on that path).

tasks.title: The window
tasks.brief:
wiztry/app.py, tkinter + ttk, a light Windows look like WizTree (ttk theme "vista", falling back to "clam"; white panes; selection #cce8ff).
- bar(pct): round(pct/10) full blocks \u2588 then light blocks \u2591 to 10 cells, a space, then f"{pct:5.1f}%". shade(color, k): k < 1 darkens (each channel * k, int), k > 1 lightens (v + (255 - v) * (k - 1), int, max 255).
- class App(tk.Tk) with App(start_path=""): title WizTry, 1200x800. Toolbar: path Entry bound to self.path_var (StringVar, starts with start_path), Browse... (askdirectory), Scan (self.scan_btn), Top (zoom_top), status Label bound to self.status (StringVar).
- Below, a vertical ttk.Panedwindow: on top a horizontal one with self.tree (ttk.Treeview, columns pct, size, items, files, folders, modified; headings Name, % of Parent, Size, Items, Files, Folders, Modified) and self.types (ttk.Treeview: Extension in #0 with a 12x12 color swatch image, Size, %, Files); at the bottom self.canvas (tk.Canvas, white).
- start_scan(path): if self.busy return; set busy, disable Scan, run scanner.scan in a threading.Thread that only stores its result (top, skipped, seconds) on self; a main-thread after() loop shows "Scanning... N files" and, when the result is there, fills everything, sets busy False and the status to f"{files:,} files, {folders:,} folders, {human(size)} in {secs:.1f} s".
- Tree: one top row for the scanned folder (text = its name), open, showing its children; deeper folders get a placeholder child and fill in on <<TreeviewOpen>>. Row values: bar(% of parent size), human(size), items (files + folders), files, folders (blank for files), modified as %Y-%m-%d %H:%M. Keep self.nodes = {item id: Node}. Double-click a folder row: zoom into it. A single click on a row only selects it: self.view is always a folder (never a file), so a later resize still redraws the treemap.
- Types: one row per ext_rows() entry (text = " " + ext), largest first. self.colors = color_map(summary(...)["by_ext"]).
- draw_treemap(): clear the canvas and self.blocks; lay out self.view with treemap.layout over the canvas size (800x300 if the canvas is under 10 px, e.g. hidden); folders as an outline rectangle (#707070, no fill); files as a rectangle filled with the extension's color (OTHER if unknown), outline shade(color, 0.6), plus a cushion: a light line along the top-left (shade 1.45) and a dark line along the bottom-right (shade 0.75) when the block is over 4 px - draw the cushion lines AFTER the filled rectangle so they sit on top and show. Before a folder's children, fill the folder's area with a plain #c8c8c8 rectangle (no outline), so files too small to draw leave gray, not white holes (the canvas stays covered). Draw in layout order: a folder's gray goes down BEFORE its own files, so the colored file blocks stay on top and visible - never paint folder fills after the files. Record self.blocks[rectangle item] = file Node. Cap at 20,000 blocks by raising min_px. Redraw on window resize (debounced).
- node_at(x, y): the file Node of the block under the point, or None. tooltip_text_at(x, y): f"{node.path}\n{human(node.size)}" or "". Mouse motion shows that text in a small yellow label near the pointer; click selects the node in the tree.
- select_node(node): open its parent rows (filling placeholders), select and show its row, return the item id. zoom(node): self.view = node and redraw. zoom_top(): back to self.top. Keep self.top (scanned root) and self.view.
- main(): App().mainloop().

tasks.title: The portable exe
tasks.brief: build.bat at the top of the project: cd to its own folder; use the Python in the WIZTRY_PY environment variable when it is set, else .venv\Scripts\python.exe; run `-m PyInstaller --onefile --windowed --name WizTry --noconfirm --clean --distpath dist --workpath build --specpath build WizTry.py`; exit 1 if that fails or dist\WizTry.exe is missing. .gitignore already ignores dist/ and build/. The test builds it (about a minute), then runs dist\WizTry.exe --scan on the fixture with no Python on the PATH and checks the report.

tasks.title: Folder paths as people type them
tasks.brief:
Typing C: and scanning must scan the drive, not the folder the program was started from (os.path.abspath("C:") is the current folder on C:).
- wiztry/scanner.py: add clean_root(path: str) -> str. Strip spaces, then one pair of surrounding double quotes, then spaces again. Nothing left -> return "". Turn forward slashes into backslashes. Exactly a drive letter and a colon ("C:" or "c:") -> that drive's root, upper-case, with the backslash ("C:\\"). Anything else -> os.path.abspath of it (that also drops a trailing backslash, except on a drive root). It never checks that the folder exists.
- scan() calls clean_root on its root in place of os.path.abspath, so every caller gets it.
- wiztry/cli.py: use clean_root in place of os.path.abspath for --scan.
- Change nothing else: every check in tests/test_scanner.py and tests/test_cli.py must keep passing.

tasks.title: A window that works as opened
tasks.brief:
Three faults a person hits in the first minute. Fix them in wiztry/app.py and change nothing else about how the window works; every check in tests/test_app.py must keep passing.
1. Browse does nothing. The code calls tk.filedialog, which does not exist until tkinter.filedialog is imported: add `import tkinter.filedialog` at the top and call tkinter.filedialog.askdirectory(parent=self). Make the method public: browse(). The Browse... button calls it. If the dialog returns "" (Cancel), change nothing. Otherwise put clean_root(answer) in self.path_var (the dialog answers with forward slashes; the box shows backslashes) and start the scan at once, the same way the Scan button does.
2. The Scan button. Take clean_root(self.path_var.get()) (from wiztry.scanner). Empty -> start nothing and set self.status to "Type a folder or press Browse... first". Not an existing folder (os.path.isdir) -> start nothing and set self.status to f"Folder not found: {path}". Otherwise write the cleaned path back into self.path_var and call start_scan(path).
3. With no start_path, the path box starts with the system drive's root: os.environ.get("SystemDrive", "C:") + "\\". App(start_path) with a path keeps that path, as now.
4. The File Types list starts 1 pixel wide because the panes were added to the ttk.PanedWindows without weights. Give them weights: in the vertical one, the top row weight=2 and the treemap weight=3; in the horizontal one, the tree weight=3 and the File Types list weight=1. At 1200x800 the list must be at least 250 px wide, the tree at least 500 px and the wider of the two, the treemap at least 250 px high.
To look at sizes yourself, never show the window on the desktop: app.geometry("1200x800+-4000+-4000"), then app.update() for half a second, then read winfo_width().

tasks.title: A treemap layout that scales
tasks.brief:
The layout takes minutes on a folder with 300,000 files, and with thousands of entries it makes slivers too thin to draw. Two changes in wiztry/treemap.py and one in wiztry/app.py; squarify()'s and layout()'s arguments and return values stay exactly as they are, and every check in tests/test_treemap.py must keep passing.

1. Replace _squarify_impl with the standard squarified algorithm, in ONE pass with running totals. No list slicing, no pop(0), no list copies, no sum() over a row or over the remainder inside a loop: those made it quadratic. Delete the helpers it no longer needs (_all_equal, _grid_layout, _next_row, _row_ar, _worst_ar).
   scale = w * h / total turns a size into an area in pixels. Keep an index i into sizes. While items remain and w > 0 and h > 0: side = min(w, h). Start a row with item i: row_sum = its area, lo = hi = its area, worst = max(side*side*hi / row_sum**2, row_sum**2 / (side*side*lo)). Try the next item j: with new_sum, new_lo, new_hi compute new_worst the same way; if new_worst > worst stop the row, otherwise take the item and go on. Then thick = row_sum / side. If w >= h the row is a column at the left: each item gets (x, cy, thick, area / thick) with cy running down from y; then x += thick and w -= thick. Otherwise it is a row along the top: each item gets (cx, y, area / thick, thick) with cx running right from x; then y += thick and h -= thick. Return the rectangles in the order of sizes.

2. layout() must only lay out children that can be seen, and must not inflate them. With children = the node's children of size > 0 and total_size = their sum: need = min_px * min_px * total_size / (w * h). Keep only the children with size >= need (a block needs at least min_px by min_px of area). If more than MAX_CHILDREN = 4000 are left (a module constant), keep the 4000 largest. If none are left return []. Sort the kept ones largest first. rest = total_size minus the sum of the kept sizes. If rest > 0, insert rest as ONE extra entry into the list of sizes at the place its size puts it (before the first size smaller than it, or at the end), call squarify, and throw that entry's rectangle away, so every kept child keeps its true share of the area. The rest of layout() (the min_px test on each rectangle, going into folders with the 1 px inset, depth) stays as it is.

3. One change in wiztry/app.py, in draw_treemap() ONLY (touch nothing else in that file). The new layout returns many more blocks, and the old cap there (a ladder that calls layout again with min_px 5, 7, 10, 15) then ends with no file blocks at all, which fails tests/test_app.py ("50,000 files stay within the 20,000-block cap"). Replace the ladder by: ONE call layout(self.view, 0, 0, cw, ch); if there are more than MAX_BLOCKS = 8000 file blocks (a module constant in app.py), keep the 8000 with the largest area (width * height) and drop the other file blocks; folder blocks are all kept. Then draw exactly as now. Every check in tests/test_app.py must keep passing: run it too before you finish.

tasks.title: The window stays alive on big folders
tasks.brief:
Scanning a drive made the window hang. Four changes in wiztry/app.py; everything else about the window stays, and every check in tests/test_app.py and tests/test_window_use.py must keep passing.

1. Count while scanning. start_scan sets self.scan_count = 0. The scan thread calls timed_scan(path, progress) from wiztry.scanner (it returns (top, skipped, seconds)), where progress(n) only stores n in self.scan_count (a plain attribute: the thread never touches tkinter). While the result is not there, the after() loop sets the status to f"Scanning... {self.scan_count:,} files" whenever self.scan_count is above 0 (plain "Scanning..." before that).

2. No second walk on the main thread. Still in the scan thread, after the scan: by_ext = summary(top)["by_ext"] (summary is in wiztry.scanner). The thread stores (top, skipped, seconds, by_ext) for the main thread. Delete _get_by_ext, _accumulate_ext and _timed_scan.

3. A public method show_result(self, top, skipped, secs, by_ext), run on the main thread by the after() loop once the result is there (after it has set busy False and enabled Scan). It does what the end of the scan does today: self.top = top, self.view = top, self.nodes = {}, self.colors = color_map(by_ext), empty and fill the tree (top row open, as now), fill the File Types list from by_ext, draw the treemap, and set the status to f"{top.files:,} files, {top.folders:,} folders, {human(top.size)} in {secs:.1f} s". It must work when called directly with a tree made in memory, and it must not walk the whole tree.

4. Swatches. The File Types list keeps only its last PhotoImage (self.types.image = img), so every other swatch is garbage-collected and shows blank. Keep them all: self.swatches = [] when the list is emptied, self.swatches.append(img) for every row.

The block cap in draw_treemap (MAX_BLOCKS) was already changed by T09: leave it as it is.
